source_evidence.anchor: Original Samplinglib supplement: The algebraic sphere-generator identity. Exact assumptions and formula below.
source_evidence.statement: Fix a unit vector \(w\in\mathbb R^I\), a real function \(f\), an ambient vector \(u\), and \(\lambda\ge0\). Interpret \(Df\) and \(D^2f\) as the total Fréchet-derivative operators used in Lean. With projected columns \(p_j=e_j-w_jw\), the displayed algebraic equality holds. For a C² ambient test near the unit sphere, it is the usual identity for the Itô generator with noise columns \(\sqrt{2\lambda}\,p_j\) and radial drift \(-\lambda(d-1)w\), where \(d=|I|\).
assumptions: The coordinate set is finite with decidable equality, $\|w\|=1$, and $\lambda\ge 0$.

The vector \(u\) is arbitrary. No smoothness hypothesis is needed for the total-derivative algebra equality. The interpretation as a classical generator requires a C² ambient test; when \(u\) is also tangent, its first-order term is the directional derivative of the restricted test.
The operators are total: Lean assigns zero to a Fréchet derivative where differentiability fails. The classical derivative interpretation is only asserted under the smooth-test qualification above.
source_evidence.boundary: The result is a pointwise identity for total derivative operators at one unit state, including temperature zero. Its classical generator interpretation uses the downstream C² test assumptions; its restricted directional-derivative interpretation also uses tangent u.

steps.title: Remove the noise amplitude from the trace
steps.mathematical_move: The Hessian is bilinear and the square root is taken of a nonnegative number. Squaring the amplitude and multiplying by one half gives the temperature.

steps.title: Combine the radial drift and Hessian
steps.mathematical_move: The projected trace removes one radial Hessian entry. The radial drift gives the first-derivative term with factor $d-1$.
